subject: Lab network priming and staged fallback notes
messages:
From: Harriet Ng <harriet.ng@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, ACME Cloud Infra <cloud-infra@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Lab network priming & staged fallback plan

Hi Mina and team,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we sign off our internal change window I'd like a concise list of the small-batch priming steps we discussed for the lab racks and the fallback ladder we will use if we see routing instability. My ops lead asked for:

- Exact KV-cache warmup sequence (per-region).
- What health-probe thresholds will mark an automatic fallback vs require manual intervention.
- A one-page runbook we can hand to on-call for the 2am window.

Can you share the final artifacts and confirm the 2am–4am PT test window on Monday 11/01?

Also confirm whether you will provision extra N+1 capacity for the first 6 hours post-priming.

Best,
Harriet Ng
Senior Cloud Engineer, ACME Industries
[Attachment: acme_preflight_checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Harriet Ng <harriet.ng@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 12:06:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lab network priming & staged fallback plan

Harriet — thanks for the clear list. Attached are the artifacts you requested and notes below. We can absolutely do the 2am–4am PT window on Monday 11/01; I will be on the bridge.

Summary (high-level):
- KV-cache warmup: three phases per region — cold load (index only), steady prefix load (10% traffic profile), ramp to 50% simulated tokens for 20 minutes. See kv_cache_warmup_steps.md attached.
- Health probes and thresholds: 5xx rate > 1% for two consecutive 1-minute windows triggers auto-fallback to standby model variant; RTT p50 > 500ms for 3 minutes triggers alert but not automatic fallback.
- Fallback ladder: primary -> quantized-primary -> regional-standby -> global-standby. See fallback-ladder.csv attached.
- Capacity: we'll provision one extra GPU per availability zone (N+1) for the first 6 hours. Ops will monitor token throughput and manually scale if we hit sustained queueing.

Runbook highlights (attached runbook_v2.pdf):
- Pre-window checks (30m): BGP adjacency, VLAN validation, health-probe sanity, KV priming dry-run.
- Execution (0m): Start KV cold load (script), monitor token queue and p95 latency.
- If p95 latency climbs > 900ms OR queue depth > 300 for 5 minutes -> execute staged fallback step 1 (switch to quantized-primary).
- Escalation path: on-call -> Mina -> Platform Eng -> Account Eng.

Bridge schedule:
- 01:30 PT bridge open (greenroom), 02:00 PT priming starts, 03:30 PT quick validation, 04:00 PT bridge close.

Attachments: runbook_v2.pdf, kv_cache_warmup_steps.md, fallback-ladder.csv

Quick ask: Connor, can you confirm the rollback window and the expected DNS TTL behavior (we discussed 60s but I want that in writing)?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook_v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Harriet Ng <harriet.ng@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:24:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lab network priming & staged fallback plan

On Fri, Oct 30, 2026 at 12:06 PM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick ask: Connor, can you confirm the rollback window and the expected DNS TTL behavior (we discussed 60s but I want that in writing)?

Confirming:
- Rollback window: first 45 minutes after priming start we will hold the fast path; after 45m a graduated rollback may be executed (we'll move traffic back to previous routing set in two steps).
- DNS TTL: we'll set the edge-route TTL to 60s for the duration of the window and restore to 300s at 06:00 PT after validation. Ops will push the TTL change 20 minutes before the bridge open.

One more callout: we should add a small synthetic client test that hits the regional-standby variant directly to validate correctness of responses after failover — I'll add a one-shot job to the runbook.

Connor O'Brien
SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: synthetic-test-snippet.sh (SH)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Harriet Ng <harriet.ng@acme-corp.com>, ACME Cloud Infra <cloud-infra@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: FINAL: Lab priming checklist + bridge + post-priming validation

Harriet — good to go for Monday 11/01 02:00–04:00 PT. Final notes and what we'll run on the bridge: 

1) Pre-bridge (01:30): BGP/ACL quick pass, KV dry-run, health probes sanity (Connor)
2) 02:00: start cold-load -> prefix ramp -> 50% simulated tokens for 20m
3) 02:25: run synthetic direct-check against regional-standby (Connor's job)
4) 02:40: decision point: if no regressions, continue ramp; if regressions, execute fallback ladder step 1; if regressions persist after step 2, run full rollback (45m window rule applies)
5) 03:30: quick functional validation (sample user prompts), compare outputs against baseline; if OK, begin scaled traffic drain
6) Post-priming (04:00–06:00): monitor telemetry; restore DNS TTL to 300s at 06:00 PT

I'll be on the primary bridge line and will send a short post-priming email with a pass/fail and any follow-ups. Attached artifacts are the runbook and the warmup script. Please review offline and let us know if you want additional rollback steps added to the ladder.

Thanks all — see you on the bridge.

Mina Haddad
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: runbook_v2.pdf, kv_cache_warmup_steps.md, fallback-ladder.csv]
